topic: AIによる職場モニタリングと働く人への影響

sources.exact_title: Algorithmic management in the workplace: New evidence from an OECD employer survey
sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

pages_used.support: Table 1 lists instruction, monitoring, and evaluation uses, including allocating work, monitoring completion/time/speed, and setting targets.
Main findings report managers' perceived decision-making benefits and identify increased information available for decisions as one mechanism.

sources.exact_title: Artificial intelligence for worker management: implications for occupational safety and health
sources.publisher: European Agency for Safety and Health at Work

pages_used.support: Defines AI worker management as data-driven systems used to allocate work and shifts and monitor or evaluate worker behaviour and performance; describes task-allocation opportunities and autonomy or workload risks.
Calls for transparency, human control, dialogue, worker consultation, and participation in design and implementation.

sources.exact_title: The Algorithmic Management of work and its implications in different contexts

pages_used.support: Describes allocation, direction, monitoring, evaluation, discipline, and reward as algorithmic-management functions.
Discusses autonomy and discretion as job-quality dimensions affected by pervasive monitoring and algorithmic instructions.
Discusses work intensity and workload implications.
Discusses transparency, human monitoring, and worker consultation as governance needs.
